### 1 — Scene
A breakfast plate with scrambled eggs, bacon, pineapple, blueberries, and what appears to be chia pudding.

### 2 — Vessel
A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Using a 26 cm circular approximation, its area is **3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
Scrambled eggs, one curved strip of bacon, pineapple chunks, blueberries, and apparent chia pudding. No separate oil, dressing, or sauce is visibly measurable.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
Heights represent average pile thickness; bulk densities account for gaps.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrambled eggs | 28% | 149 cm² × 1.3 cm = 194 ml | 0.95 | 184 g | 160 | 294 kcal |
| Bacon | 4% | 21 cm² × 0.7 cm = 15 ml | 0.90 | 13 g | 500 | 65 kcal |
| Pineapple | 17% | 90 cm² × 2.0 cm = 180 ml | 0.60 | 108 g | 50 | 54 kcal |
| Blueberries | 5% | 27 cm² × 1.5 cm = 40 ml | 0.65 | 26 g | 57 | 15 kcal |
| Chia pudding, apparent | 18% | 96 cm² × 1.2 cm = 115 ml | 1.00 | 115 g | 120 | 138 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 28 + 4 + 17 + 5 + 18 = **72%**, consistent with the visible uncovered plate.

### 8 — Sanity check
The estimate is **446 g and approximately 566 kcal**, plausible for this moderately full breakfast plate. The pudding’s identity and recipe are the largest energy uncertainties; egg preparation also affects calories.
